summary: The legal integer has at most ten decimal digits, so its complete source domain is too tightly bounded for a reliable runtime-scaling verdict.

workload_bound.source_constraint: n is an integer from 1 through 10^9 inclusive

replacement_checks.evidence: Each outer-loop iteration removes one decimal digit, and every digit name contains at most five letters, so any legal execution performs at most ten digit iterations and fifty bit toggles.
Authored cases cover one-digit inputs, repeated digits, embedded zeros, nine-digit patterns, distinct nonzero digits, and the ten-digit upper boundary.
